learning_outcomes.text: To know the different systems and equipment existing in which ELECTRICITY, GAS and PLUMBING installations can be based, analyzing their characteristics from the different points of view that an Engineer must consider to carry out the design of a specific installation: needs that the installation must meet, technical feasibility of its realization, restrictions imposed by regulations, environmental impact, energy efficiency, economic cost, future maintenance requirements, etc.

Acquisition during theoretical classes of an awareness regarding the constructive, technical and execution characteristics of the various constituent elements of industrial installations included in the program.
To be able to calculate all the elements involved in these installations.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and succinct presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for seeking sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability to work collaboratively and capacity for developing multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and an open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the field of Industrial Engineering, based on acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.
Development of autonomy and creativity capacities, fostering aptitudes for developing one's own initiatives and undertaking new projects.
Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

syllabus_topics: INDUSTRIAL ACTIVITY.- Introduction. Types of industrial activities. The Engineer in Industry.
STANDARDS FOR INDUSTRIAL INSTALLATIONS.- Processing. Standards for specific industries. Industrial register. Requirements an industry must meet. Investments.
INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY.- Basic requirements. Processing. Record maintenance. Quality and manufacturing mark. Product certification.
INTRODUCTION TO ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS.- Low Voltage Electrotechnical Regulation. Company-specific standards. Conduction, cabling, and installation materials in Low Voltage.

GENERAL ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS.- Notions of low voltage distribution networks. Electrical connections. General protection boxes. Measurement equipment. Individual branches. Distribution boards. Notions of conductor calculation. Circuit design.

CALCULATION OF ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS. Generalities. Load calculation. Line calculation. Protection calculation. Distribution of equipment and mechanisms. Earthing. Plans and diagrams. Regulations. LIGHTING. Generalities. Introduction. Types of lighting and luminaires. Lighting calculation. Luminaire distribution. Plans and diagrams. Regulations.

SPECIAL ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS I.- Installations in public premises. Installations with fire and explosion risk. Installations in humid premises. Installations in wet premises. Installations in other premises with special characteristics.
GENERAL CONCEPTS ON GAS INSTALLATIONS. Concepts. Basic terminology. Classification of gases. Fundamental properties of gases. Gas liquefaction.

REGULATIONS AND NORMATIVES. Scope of application. Definitions. Installations requiring a project. Documents for commissioning installations. Technical Instructions. Typical diagrams of receiving installations.

DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION.- Components, distribution, connection, and consumption appliances. Conduits. Pipe routing requirements. Criteria for placement of elements and accessories. Construction of receiving installations. Documentation and commissioning of gas receiving installations.

CALCULATION OF RECEIVING INSTALLATIONS.- Basic data for the calculation of receiving installations. Allowable pressure drop, minimum diameters. Magnitudes and units. Graphic representations. Plans and diagrams of plumbing installations.

CONDITIONS FOR LOCATION AND CONNECTION OF GAS APPLIANCES.- Types of gas appliances. Configuration of the premises where they are located. Evacuation of combustion products. Installation conditions for appliances. Cathodic protection of gas installations.
BOILERS, burners, and chimneys. Valves and various devices in gas installations. Safety devices.
PLANS AND INTERPRETATION.- Graphic representations. Projections and views. Building plans. Representation of measurements. Use of symbols in plans.

TESTS AND VERIFICATIONS.- Pressure tests and commissioning. Watertightness test of receiving installations. Classification of defects in gas installations in service. Connection certificates. Installation and review of gas installations and appliances.
BASIC CONCEPTS OF LIGHT. Light. Color. Luminous magnitudes of electric lamps. Luminous units. Fundamental principles.

LAMPS: Characteristics and properties of lamps. Incandescent lamps. Halogen incandescent lamps. Fluorescent lamps or tubes. Mercury vapor discharge lamps. Sodium vapor discharge lamps. Induction lamps. Metal halide lamps. LED lamps.
LUMINAIRES: Classification of luminaires. Degree of protection of luminaires. Lighting diagrams. Basic photometric data. Luminaire efficiency.
AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT.- Auxiliary regulation and control equipment. Ballasts. Starters. Capacitors. Energy-saving equipment. Electrical equipment for different lamps.

INTERIOR LIGHTING: Lighting level. Lighting design. Calculation of interior lighting. Lighting performance. Recommended lighting levels. Maintenance factor. Regulation and control systems for interior lighting installations.

EXTERIOR LIGHTING: Outdoor lighting. ITC BT 09 Instruction of the Low Voltage Electrotechnical Regulation 'Outdoor lighting installations'. Calculation of outdoor lighting by the luminous flux method. Utilization curves. Regulation and control systems for outdoor lighting installations. Maintenance.
NEW LIGHTING SYSTEMS: LED lighting.
Energy efficiency of lighting installations. Efficient regulation and control systems in lighting installations (interior and exterior). Regulation on energy efficiency of outdoor lighting.
teaching_methods: Theoretical academic sessions (lectures) with oral presentation of theoretical content supported by computer systems.
Practical classroom sessions for solving practical exercises related to theoretical content.
Seminars for correcting completed practical assignments.
Online monitoring activities via the Studium platform.
Problem-solving: Solving exercises related to the course syllabus.
assessment_rules: Assessment includes an in-person exam of theoretical and practical knowledge, guided practical assignments, personalized tutorials, a practical exam, and continuous assessment. Attendance at in-person theoretical and practical classes is required, as is the mandatory submission of assigned work. Students are recommended to study, solve exercises and problems throughout the course, submit assigned work continuously, and use tutorials.
